results.name: 4 Reverse Lunge and 4 Side Taps
instructions: Start with feet shoulder-width apart, arms straight in front of your torso.
Step your right foot back into a reverse lunge, bending both knees to 90 degrees. Return to the starting position by stepping your right foot forward and repeat 1 time.
Return to standing position and perform four side taps by stepping your right foot out to the side and tapping the floor, then bringing it back to the center. Repeat on the other side.
Return to starting position and repeat.
tips: Keep your core muscles engaged to maintain balance and stability during lunges and taps.
Perform each lunge and tap with control to maximize muscle activation and minimize injury risk.
Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your front foot during lunges to avoid unnecessary strain on your knee joint.
results.description: 4 Reverse Lunge and 4 Side Taps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Alternate Single Leg Raise Plank
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lift your right leg off the floor, extending it straight back while maintaining the plank position. Hold briefly.
Lower your right leg back to the starting position.
Lift your left leg off the floor, extending it straight back. Hold briefly before lowering it back to the starting position. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and prevent your hips from sagging.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels, avoiding any arching or rounding of your back.
results.description: Alternate Single Leg Raise Plank is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Alternating Step Out
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lift one of your feet off the floor and step to your side.
Return to the initial position and do the same with your other foot. Repeat.
tips: Focus on keeping your upper body upright and avoid leaning too far forward or backward.
Use a steady pace to maintain a rhythm, which will help with coordination and balance.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you step out and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Alternating Step Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Adductors.

results.name: Ankle Dorsal Flexion
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands resting on your hips or at your sides for balance.
Flex both feet simultaneously, bringing your toes towards your shins, and then return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement, flexing and relaxing both feet simultaneously.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on the movement of your ankles and avoid using your leg muscles to assist.
results.description: Ankle Dorsal Flexion is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Ankle Plantar Flexion
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands resting on your hips or at your sides for balance..
Rise onto your toes, lifting your heels off the floor.
Lower your heels back to the starting position. Repeat the movement.
tips: Keep your knees slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints and enhance stability.
Use a mirror to check your form and ensure that your ankles are aligned properly.
Focus on maintaining a steady breathing pattern, exhaling as you rise and inhaling as you lower.
results.description: Ankle Plantar Flexion is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

results.name: Ankle Circles
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, hands at your hips.
Lift your right foot off the floor slightly and rotate your ankle in a circular motion, making small controlled circles.
After a set number of rotations, switch direction and rotate your ankle in the opposite direction.
Repeat the movement with your left ankle, rotating in both directions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Ensure your leg remains still and only your ankle is moving to focus on the targeted muscles.
Perform the exercise for an equal amount of time or repetitions in both directions to ensure balanced muscle development.
results.description: Ankle Circles is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

results.name: Ankle Pumps
instructions: Sit or lie with your legs straight.
Point your toes away from you as far as you comfortably can.
Pull your toes back toward your shins.
Keep alternating in a slow, steady rhythm.
tips: Useful for circulation and ankle mobility.
Move through the full range.
results.description: Ankle Pumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category.

results.name: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand facing away from an elevated box and place your right foot on it. Hold onto a stable bar or support in front of you with your right hand. Keep your chest upright and your front foot flat on the floor.
Lower your body by bending your front knee and hip until your back knee is close to the floor.
Pause for a second at the bottom and push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up.
Do not let your front knee travel excessively past your toes to reduce joint stress.
Maintain an upright torso to keep the tension on your quads and glutes.
results.description: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Assisted Pistol Squats
instructions: Stand upright while holding onto a sturdy equipment with both hands for balance. Extend one leg straight forward and keep it off the floor while the other leg remains on the floor.
Lower yourself slowly by bending the standing leg at the hip and knee, keeping your chest up and your extended leg straight in front of you.
Descend until your glutes are close to your heel and then push through the heel of your planted foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Lower yourself slowly and avoid collapsing at the bottom of the squat to avoid injury.
Extend your non-working leg fully in front of you and keep it parallel to the floor.
Use your arms only for assistance, not to pull yourself up or down.
results.description: Assisted Pistol Squats is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Back Forward Leg Swings
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and use a nearby support (such as a squat cage, wall or a chair) for balance.
Swing your right leg forward and backward in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
After completing the desired number of swings with your right leg, switch to your left leg and repeat the movement.
Focus on smooth and controlled swings, avoiding excessive momentum.
tips: Focus on maintaining a steady rhythm to ensure controlled movements.
Ensure your upper body remains upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
Keep your supporting leg slightly bent to enhance balance and reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: Back Forward Leg Swings is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.
